aidb_assessment.novelty: High conceptual novelty in evaluation design: the work combines executable repository outcomes with a matched memory toggle and explicitly separates availability of useful history from construction and retrieval by memory systems. Outcome-based selection is also an unusual way to guarantee that every retained target contains demonstrably useful prior experience, though it narrows external validity.
aidb_assessment.rationale: Adopt VibeMemBench as a diagnostic evaluation suite, contingent on verifying the released artifacts and reproducing a subset of runs. Do not adopt its aggregate transfer scores as deployment forecasts. The controlled design and consequential negative results are decision-relevant, but all principal transfer intervals cross zero, target selection is intentionally favorable to useful memory, and the tested systems and solver families are limited.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: High for researchers and engineers designing coding-agent memory. The benchmark offers controlled baselines, negative results, diagnostics, and concrete design implications: gate injection by headroom, compress raw transcripts around repair spans, preserve target-anchored constraints, and do not assume more retrieved records will solve form degradation. It is less suitable for estimating real-world average memory uplift because targets are selected for positive reference uplift.

executive_summary: VibeMemBench is a carefully controlled benchmark for asking whether persistent memory improves executable repository work, rather than merely recalling stored facts. It selects targets for which a target-aware historical experience helped a reference solver, freezes that experience, transfers it to held-out solvers, and separately tests four existing memory systems on the same histories. The strongest conclusion is a gap between available and delivered experience: verified records produce small directional gains for most transfer solvers and reduce steps for all, whereas almost every system–solver retrieval pairing fails to beat memory-off. However, all transfer confidence intervals cross zero, the benchmark is deliberately outcome-selected, and proprietary frontier solvers are absent. The evidence therefore supports using the benchmark as a diagnostic and design testbed, not treating its aggregate uplift as an unbiased deployment estimate. Its most actionable findings are that uniform injection can harm already-capable solvers, record form matters more than simple ranking expansion, and raw transcript volume appears more damaging than instruction semantics alone.

assumptions: Passing the declared executable predicate is an adequate measure of target resolution.
The fixed reference agent and shortlist are sufficient to certify the existence of at least one useful historical experience, although not the globally best one.
Paired runs under the same declared configuration isolate the memory intervention apart from stochastic seed variation.
Pre-trajectory top-ranked retrieval is a meaningful evaluation of existing memory systems, even though it does not model online closed-loop memory.
Target-level bootstrap resampling with seeds kept intact is the appropriate uncertainty unit.
key_components: SIEVE source validation, same-repository patch-pattern screening, history execution and target-aware experience distillation, followed by retention based on positive reference uplift.
A frozen verified record containing a bug class, root cause, fix pattern, and reusable lesson, constructed without access to the target gold patch, test patch, or test outcome.
A matched intervention contract in which only declared persistence and retrieval may differ between memory-off and memory-on conditions.
Two evaluation layers: direct transfer of frozen verified experience, and retrieval from full eligible history by four existing memory systems.
Diagnostic analyses covering headroom, first-broken-stage attribution, record-form mechanisms, same-record cross-solver contrasts, stripping, retrieval-budget dose, and counterfactual substitution.
method.overview: The authors construct VibeMemBench with the four-stage SIEVE pipeline. Source instances are validated by executing their gold patches; prior tasks from the same repository are screened using patch structure and an LLM judgment; selected history trajectories are executed and distilled into target-aware records; and targets are retained only when some candidate record improves a reference solver over memory-off. Evaluation then pairs memory-on and memory-off runs while fixing the task, seed, agent, prompt, tools, sandbox, budget, task order, and aggregation. One layer transfers each frozen selected record to held-out solvers. A second layer lets Mem0, SimpleMem, MemoryOS, and A-MEM ingest eligible histories and inject their top-ranked record. Executable test resolution is primary; solver tokens and agent steps are secondary. Target-level bootstrap intervals retain all seeds of each target.

open_questions: Can solver headroom be estimated before executing a full memory-off trajectory accurately enough to gate retrieval safely?
Does a target-anchored repair schema trained specifically on coding trajectories outperform raw transcript and dialogue-fact schemas under the same token budget?
Would a token-matched irrelevant control alter the interpretation of the frozen-record transfer gains?
How stable are the findings across new repositories, chronological releases, online retrieval during solving, and proprietary frontier solvers?
Can confidence-calibrated abstention from memory injection preserve below-ceiling gains while avoiding ceiling losses?

problem.importance: A memory system may retrieve plausible or relevant text yet fail to improve—and may even degrade—the only downstream outcome that ultimately matters: whether the modified repository passes its declared executable tests.
problem.scope: The paper evaluates persistent-memory interventions on repository-level bug fixes, features, interface changes, configuration work, and related tasks. It studies frozen verified-experience transfer and pre-trajectory retrieval, not online closed-loop memory during a target-solving trajectory.
problem.statement: Existing repository benchmarks measure executable code changes without isolating persistent memory, while memory benchmarks measure recall without establishing whether retrieved experience improves repository repair.

proposed_experiments.baseline: Uniform top-ranked injection and memory-off, evaluated on the same target–seed pairs. Train or calibrate the gate without using each evaluation target’s realized memory-off outcome.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: A prospective headroom gate can retain most gains on difficult targets while reducing harm on targets the solver already resolves reliably.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Paired change in Resolved versus memory-off, accompanied by the share of injected targets, ceiling-target losses, below-ceiling gains, and target-level bootstrap intervals.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop if the gated condition fails to improve the uniform-injection point estimate and fails to reduce ceiling losses, or if its interval excludes the prespecified minimum useful gain on the unfavorable side.

proposed_experiments.baseline: MemoryOS or A-MEM raw-transcript records, Mem0 or SimpleMem atomic records, and a token-matched irrelevant-text control, all using the same retrieved source history.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Target-anchored extraction that emits root cause, repair action, constraints, and code anchors will outperform raw transcripts and dialogue-fact records under equal context allocation.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Paired Resolved difference under a fixed token budget; secondary diagnostics are form-degradation rate, retained repair-field rate, solver tokens, and steps.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop if the structured extractor does not beat both memory-system families on paired Resolved or if any apparent gain disappears against the token-matched control.

proposed_experiments.baseline: The paper’s pre-trajectory top-ranked condition, memory-off, and frozen verified experience under matched total context and resource budgets.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Online, confidence-triggered retrieval during the solver trajectory is more useful than pre-trajectory top-ranked injection because it can condition records on the solver’s observed state and avoid unnecessary context.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Paired Resolved difference, with memory-side and solver-side tokens, latency, retrieval count, and ceiling-target harm recorded separately.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop if online retrieval does not exceed pre-trajectory retrieval in Resolved or if additional memory-side cost exceeds a prespecified budget without a compensating success gain.

artifacts: The paper states that the release preserves target provenance, test commands, environments, and execution results.
The release manifest is described as recording construction variants, prompts, chronology, model revisions, retrieval configuration, target queries, and condition fields.
Task histories, executable predicates, intervention protocol, injected text, retrieval events, trajectory paths, and declared agent steps are described as released or logged.
Failure-attribution labels are described as deterministically recomputable; judge labels and disagreement cases are said to enter the release.
reproducibility.assessment: The reporting contract is unusually detailed and repeatedly states what the release contains, including executable predicates, environments, manifests, provenance, and recomputable diagnostics. However, the supplied material does not expose the release itself or an immutable artifact reference, so artifact completeness and end-to-end rerunnability cannot be verified here. Reproducibility is therefore partial rather than strong.

The supplied blocks do not include the actual manifests, container hashes, source code, prompts, or raw run files needed to verify reproducibility claims directly.
Memory-side token consumption, latency, wall-clock time, and API cost are not recorded.
Exact provider snapshots and continued availability of evaluated model endpoints cannot be established from the supplied document alone.

results.context: This is the strongest controlled evidence that selected historical experience can transfer beyond the reference solver, but it does not establish a reliable nonzero average effect at the benchmark’s sample size.

evidence.quote: The frozen verified experience raises Resolved on four of the five transfer solvers and leaves deepseek-v4-pro unchanged
All five bootstrap intervals cross zero, so at 111 targets the observed gains of 1.1 to 4.5 points remain directional evidence rather than effects separable from zero.

results.result: Frozen verified experience increased observed resolution for four of five held-out solvers, with changes ranging from 1.1 to 4.5 percentage points; deepseek-v4-pro was unchanged. Yet every bootstrap interval crossed zero, so these are directional rather than statistically separated effects.

results.context: The contrast between frozen-record transfer and system retrieval supports an availability-to-use gap. It also shows that shorter trajectories are not sufficient evidence of helpful memory.

evidence.quote: Eleven of the twelve solver and system pairings stay at or below the matched memory-off baseline, no system interval lies above zero, and the glm-5 and Mem0 interval lies entirely below it.
The single exception, MemoryOS on glm-5, gains 2.0 points and still trails the frozen verified experience.

results.result: Existing systems underperformed broadly: eleven of twelve solver–system pairings stayed at or below memory-off. The only positive point estimate was MemoryOS on glm-5 at 2.0 points, and its interval still crossed zero; glm-5 with Mem0 was the sole pairing whose interval lay entirely below zero.

results.context: Under the paper’s written anchor rule, retrieval usually reached related history but rendered it poorly. This attribution is mechanistically useful, though its fine categories are sensitive to how anchors are interpreted.

results.context: This is a consequential negative ablation: lexical instruction-pollution markers identify bulky records but do not isolate the harmful semantic component.

evidence.quote: The strip arm gains 0.60 resolved seeds per pairing and the random arm gains 0.48, so removing an equal count of unflagged lines recovers a comparable amount.
The harm operates through transcript volume rather than instruction semantics.

results.result: The strip ablation did not support instruction semantics as the causal mechanism: deleting flagged lines recovered 0.60 resolved seeds per pairing, while deleting an equal number of unflagged lines recovered 0.48. The authors conclude that transcript volume, rather than instruction content, explains the comparable recovery.

results.context: This argues against top-one retrieval capacity as the principal cause, at least for the tested deepseek-v4-pro–Mem0 configuration. It does not establish that larger budgets or other retrieval systems can never help.

evidence.quote: No budget reaches the memory-off baseline.

results.result: A wider Mem0 retrieval budget did not recover performance: every budget from one to five records remained below the 67.1% memory-off baseline, and the best observed budget resolved 65.5%.

title: VibeMemBench: Evaluating Memory Systems for Coding Agents on Real Repository Coding Tasks
